name: Revolut
summary: Revolut is a global financial app spanning payments, cards, deposits, wealth products, business banking, and cross-border money movement.
overview: Revolut is a London-headquartered financial platform building a multi-product bank and payments business across consumer and business customers.

facts.label: Latest disclosed valuation
facts.note: Fundraising process completed in 2025, according to the company’s 2025 annual report.

bull_case: A broad product suite, growing customer base, and improving profitability can turn Revolut into a global financial operating system.
bear_case: Bank licensing, compliance demands, regional competition, and the complexity of credit products can slow international execution.
directory_notes: Revenue, customer growth, and licensing progress

intelligence.description: Revolut is building a global financial app that combines everyday spending, payments, deposits, investing, foreign exchange, and business financial tools. Its challenge is to turn high engagement into durable, regulated banking economics across markets.
company: Revolut started with foreign-exchange and prepaid-card products, then expanded into a much broader consumer financial platform. The product now spans payments, cards, savings, investing, travel, and business financial operations, allowing the company to cross-sell from a large customer base.

The 2025 annual report describes a business whose revenue rose 46% to £4.5 billion. It also says Revolut completed a fundraising process at an implied $75 billion valuation, while continuing to invest in its regulatory and compliance capabilities as it broadens banking operations.
intelligence.why_it_matters: Revolut is a major test of whether a digital financial app can become a global, multi-product bank without losing the speed and distribution advantages of fintech. Its execution is relevant to private payments, neobanking, wealth, compliance, and infrastructure companies.

changed.text: A $800M Series E placed Revolut among Europe’s most valuable private fintechs.
A secondary transaction was reported at a $45B valuation.
Revenue rose 46% to £4.5B, according to the company’s annual report.
The company completed a fundraising process at an implied $75B valuation.

takeaways: Revolut’s value proposition is a broad financial relationship, not a single payments product.
The company reported strong 2025 revenue growth, but its valuation also assumes it can sustain growth while operating under more banking regulation.
Licenses, risk controls, and local-market operations are becoming as important as customer acquisition.
The central risk is that a globally complex product set makes economics and compliance harder to scale than a focused fintech.
